chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, who said: I heard someone narrate that he heard Ar-Rida (peace be upon him)

while he was looking at Harun in Mina or Arafat, he said: 'He and I will be buried this way,' while he pressed his two fingers together. We did not know what he meant by that until the matter concerning him in Toos occurred as it did. Then Al-Ma'mun ordered the burial of Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) next to Harun.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Rida (the title of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida)
key_terms.طُوسٍ: Toos (a city in Khorasan where the Imam was buried)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ar-Rida predict about his burial place?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Imam’s prophetic foresight by linking his burial to Harun al-Rashid, a gesture interpreted by Shia scholars as a subtle divine retribution (*muqabala*) for Harun’s role in the martyrdom of Imam Musa al-Kadhim. The narrative underscores the political and spiritual dynamics of the Abbasid era, where the Caliph’s public placement of the Imam’s grave beside his father served to legitimize his rule while fulfilling the Imam’s silent prophecy.
